fsRead.label: Read files
fsRead.desc: Can read and search files in the workspace.

terminal.label: Terminal
terminal.desc: Can run shell commands with your user's rights. While on, file and network limits can be bypassed through the shell — only for agents you trust. (Codex always runs its commands in its own sandbox; writes only inside the project folder.)

network.label: Network
network.desc: Can fetch web pages and search the internet.

browser.label: Browser
browser.desc: Not applied yet: agents can't use the in-app browser.

requireApproval.label: Require approval
requireApproval.desc: Waits for your approval before starting each task (all providers).

readonly.label: Read-only
readonly.desc: Reviews and reports; doesn't touch files.

developer.label: Developer
developer.desc: Reads and writes files; terminal and network off.

full.label: Full access
full.desc: Files, terminal, network and browser enabled.

view.title: Agents
view.subtitle: Build your team and define their duties and permissions.
view.search: Search by name, role or expertise…

empty.title: No agents yet
empty.hint: Add your first agent; you decide its name, duties and permissions.

units.title: Teams
units.desc: An agent can belong to more than one unit. It also works on the projects its units are assigned to.
units.none: Not in any unit yet. Add it to a team; once the team is assigned to a project, the agent works on that project.

new.title: New agent
new.jobDescHint: Responsibilities, scope and deliverables. The lead looks at this when assigning work.
new.jobDescPlaceholder:
e.g. Builds the mobile app screens and handles API integrations.
Deliverable: working screen + short note.
new.skillsHint: Add with Enter or a comma.
new.permNote: You can change individual permissions after creating the agent.
new.unitNote: The new agent will be added as a member of {{unit}}.
new.desksFull: The office has {{desks}} desks and they're all taken; the new agent will share a desk with another agent.

identity.title: Identity
identity.desc: Name, title and look shown in the office and in chat.
identity.activeDesc: When off, it takes no tasks and appears offline in the office.
identity.leadDescIsLead: To hand over leadership, make another agent the lead.
identity.leadDesc: Runs the chat, splits up the work, assigns and reviews it.

duty.title: Duties and job description
duty.desc: The lead uses this when distributing work; it's also added to the agent's own instructions.
duty.jobDescHint: Responsibilities, scope and deliverables. The clearer it is, the more accurate the assignments.
duty.jobDescPlaceholder:
e.g. Builds the payment and cart screens.
Responsible for form validation and error states.
Deliverable: working screen + short change note.
duty.skillsHint: Add with Enter or a comma. Tasks are matched against these tags.
duty.personaHint: How the agent should behave: tone, priorities, rules.
duty.personaPlaceholder: e.g. Writes short and clear; plans before changing anything and never ships untested work.

model.title: Model
model.desc: Which provider and model this agent runs with.
model.noProvider: No provider — runs in demo mode.

permissions.title: Permissions
permissions.desc: What this agent can access. Changes are saved instantly and stay in sync with the Permission Matrix.
permissions.extraFoldersDesc: Folders it can access in addition to the workspace. Workspace: <mono>{{path}}</mono>

danger.title: Delete agent
danger.leadBlocked: The lead can't be deleted — make another agent the lead first.
danger.desc: Assigned tasks become unassigned; run history and personal memory are deleted. This can't be undone.

duplicate.title: Duplicate
duplicate.desc: Creates a twin with the same role, job description, provider, permissions, teams, skills and access, so the lead can split work between them.
